summary: A sandstone Romanesque light station on a 361-foot rock above Big Sur, built 1887-89 with a first-order lens and still active; open by docent-led tour only.

lens.where: Removed 1978 (park history: to the Allen Knight Maritime Museum, Monterey; LighthouseFriends: loaned to the Maritime Museum of Monterey in 1992, in storage since November 2017)

structures.type: sandstone tower attached to fog-signal building

access.note: Closed except by docent-led walking tours (3 hours, 360 ft climb).

notes_for_editor: Disputes noted in text: automation 1972 vs 1974; lens removal 1978 vs 1979; cistern 69,800 vs 53,000 gallons. 1896-1897 Light-House Board volume has no page data; page numbers not given. LighthouseFriends is used for facts in own words, including the Macon testimony, which is second-hand. Henderson/Owens link not tied to roster. Fog-signal hours for 1893 to 1895 taken from OCR text by section number, not from a page image. Roster stints for Owens, Trotter and Livesay were matched by name from the USLHS list; 1919 Bulletin item gives only surnames and initials. Verifier 2026-10-22: wagon road date disagrees (NRHP 1902; Board 1900 report nearly complete, 1901 report completed); lens destination disagrees (pointsur.org 1978 to Allen Knight museum vs LighthouseFriends 1992 loan).
